why: Alma 45:18 'when Alma had done this' points at nothing; his blessing of Helaman, his sons, the land and the church (45:15-17) is skipped

bridges.Alma 45:18: Alma then blesses Helaman and his other sons, the land, and the church.

why: Alma 46:35 'he caused to be put to death' follows 46:29, whose subject is Amalickiah; the reader never sees Moroni cut off the Amalickiahites and capture them
Alma 47:3 'because of their disobedience' refers to the Lamanites' refusal (47:2) that the reader never saw
Alma 47:27 'pursue his servants' makes no sense without the frame-up of the king's servants (47:25-26); 47:24's killer is also unclear

bridges.Alma 47:27: Amalickiah's servants cry out that the king's own servants have stabbed him, and the terrified royal servants flee.

why: Alma 47:35 'the queen' appears without introduction; how Amalickiah takes the city and deceives her (47:31-34) is skipped

bridges.Alma 47:35: Amalickiah takes the city of Nephi and, with false witnesses, convinces the widowed queen that the king's own servants killed him.

why: Alma 48:23 'they were sorry to take up arms' follows praise of Moroni alone; the Nephites' reluctant return to war (48:21) is missing
Alma 51:23 drops the reader into a siege of the city of Moroni with no word that the Lamanites had invaded

bridges.Alma 51:23: While Moroni is dealing with the king-men, Amalickiah's army invades the land of Moroni on the east seacoast.

why: Alma 55:19 'this was not the desire of Moroni' points at nothing; the option of slaughtering the drunken Lamanites (55:18) is skipped, so it reads as if Moroni regretted arming the prisoners
Alma 57:12 'lose all hopes of succor' refers to a siege and captured supply train (57:8-11) the reader never saw

bridges.Alma 57:12: Helaman's army surrounds Cumeni by night and captures the supplies meant for its Lamanite defenders.

why: Alma 62:36 'the walls of the city' and the camp setting are unclear; the bridge does not say where the Lamanites are cornered

bridges.Alma 62:35: Moroni sends men and food to Helaman, retakes Nephihah by scaling its walls at night, and drives the Lamanites and King Ammoron into the land of Moroni, where his armies surround them.

why: Alma 63:8 'they were never heard of more' has no antecedent; the Nephite emigrants aboard Hagoth's ships (63:6-7) are skipped

bridges.Alma 63:8: Many Nephite families sail north in Hagoth's ship; the next year it returns and sets out again with more settlers.

why: Helaman 1:7 Paanchi appears without introduction, and 1:21 Pacumeni is suddenly chief judge; the three rival sons (1:3) and Pacumeni's succession (1:13) are skipped

bridges.Helaman 1:5: Three of his sons contend for the judgment-seat: Pahoran, Paanchi, and Pacumeni.
bridges.Helaman 1:15: Pacumeni takes his murdered brother's place as chief judge. The next year the Lamanite king sends a huge army against the Nephites.

why: Helaman 1:20 'the entrance of the city' names no city; the surprise march on poorly guarded Zarahemla (1:17-19) is skipped

bridges.Helaman 1:20: Finding the capital poorly guarded, Coriantumr's army sweeps down on Zarahemla so fast the Nephites cannot gather their forces.

why: Helaman 5:19 'Therefore they did speak ... unto the Lamanites' follows nothing, and 5:21's capture by Lamanites comes with no move into the land of Nephi
Helaman 6:17 'For behold...' follows the murder of the judges rather than the statement that the people grew wicked again (6:16)
3 Nephi 6:18 'they did wilfully rebel' follows 6:14, whose last subject is the faithful Lamanite remnant

bridges.3 Nephi 6:18: Meanwhile Satan leads the rest of the people into pride, and by the thirtieth year they are in a state of awful wickedness.
